result.topic_en: Euler derives the outflow velocity of water through a narrow tube BC with friction, shows that a sufficiently thin (capillary) tube can stop the outflow entirely, and proposes using this to determine the friction coefficient alpha experimentally.
result.transcription:
358 TENTAMEN THEORIAE

peditur, debita eſt altitudini $v=a+l-\frac{\alpha ll}{2g}$: ideoque minor eſt, quam ſi nulla adeſſet frictio.

54. In genere autem, ſi ſit $\frac{a}{f}$ tam paruum, vt prae $\frac{b}{g}$ pro nihilo reputari poſſit, erit $\mathfrak{A}=1$, $A=\frac{a}{f}$;
vnde fit $v=\frac{a e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}}+\frac{g}{\alpha}(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}})-l(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}})}{1-\frac{k^4}{g^4}(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}})}$
vnde ſi tubus BC infra penitus ſit apertus, ſeu $\frac{k^4}{g^4}=1$
erit $v=a+\frac{g}{\alpha}(e^{\frac{\alpha b}{g}}-1)-l(e^{\frac{\alpha b}{g}}-1)$

55. Si ergo tubus BC ſit tam gracilis, vt ſit $g=\alpha l$, aqua in CC maiori celeritate non effluet, quam tubo remoto in BB efflueret. Atque ſi tubus BC adhuc ſit gracilior, ſeu $g<\alpha l$, puta $g=\frac{1}{2}\alpha l$, fiet
$v=a-\frac{1}{2}l(e^{\frac{2b}{l}}-1)$
et ſi altitudo $b$ valde ſit parua prae $l$, erit
$v=a-b-\frac{bb}{l}$,
niſi ergo ſit $a>b+\frac{bb}{l}$, aqua plane non effluet, hoc eſt niſi ſit $a>b$.

56. Tubus igitur BC tam gracilis eſſe poteſt, vt frictio effluxum aquae per eius orificium CC penitus arceat, atque hinc commodiſſime valor literae $\alpha$ per experimenta explorari poterit. Inſigatur enim vaſi ſatis amplo AB, in quo aqua altitudinem $AB=a$ non nimis magnam occupat, tubus, vt vocari ſolet, capillaris, cuius amplitudine exiſtente $=gg$, ponatur $g=\frac{1}{n}\alpha l$, et cum ſit $v=a-\frac{(n-1)}{n}l(e^{\frac{nb}{l}}-1)=a-(n-1)b$;

items.quote: Si ergo tubus BC ſit tam gracilis, vt ſit $g=\alpha l$, aqua in CC maiori celeritate non effluet, quam tubo remoto in BB efflueret.
items.english: If therefore the tube BC is so thin that g = αl, the water will not flow out at CC with greater speed than it would flow out at BB with the tube removed.

items.quote: niſi ergo ſit $a>b+\frac{bb}{l}$, aqua plane non effluet, hoc eſt niſi ſit $a>b$.
items.english: Therefore unless a > b + bb/l, the water will not flow out at all, that is, unless a > b.

items.quote: atque hinc commodiſſime valor literae $\alpha$ per experimenta explorari poterit.
items.english: and hence the value of the letter α can most conveniently be determined by experiments.
